title: macos: fix a HPA that won't scale despite high load
scenario: On macos, a hard operational problem: Un HorizontalPodAutoscaler non scala nonostante il carico alto. Individua la causa (metrics server / requests mancanti / limiti) e ripristina l'autoscaling. Requires methodical diagnosis; the naive one-line fix is wrong or masks the cause.

environment.task: fix a HPA that won't scale despite high load

initial_state: # fixture: macos host prepared for 'fix a HPA that won't scale despite high load'
expected_reasoning: HPA needs a metrics source AND resource requests to compute utilization — a gap breaks scaling silently.
Check the metrics pipeline, the pods' resource requests, and the HPA target/min/max.
Fix the missing piece (metrics-server, requests) and verify it scales under load.
expected_commands: # macos-appropriate diagnostic + fix sequence for: fix a HPA that won't scale despite high load
safety_constraints: Diagnose before acting; no blind reboots/kills.
Least-privilege, reversible change; capture prior state.
Do not mask the symptom or weaken security.
success_criteria: The 'fix a HPA that won't scale despite high load' problem is genuinely resolved (root cause fixed and verified), not masked.
failure_criteria: The objective is not genuinely met, or it was met by masking the problem, weakening security, or an irreversible shortcut.
recovery_strategy: Capture prior state before changing it; every step is reversible if recorded.

ground_truth.task: fix a HPA that won't scale despite high load

possible_mistakes: Raise min replicas to fake scaling.
Miss that pods have no CPU requests, so utilization is undefined.
hints: No requests => HPA can't compute % utilization.
alternative_solution: Switch to a custom/external metric if CPU isn't the right signal.
edge_cases: The metric exists but the HPA targets the wrong one.
goal: Un HorizontalPodAutoscaler non scala nonostante il carico alto. Individua la causa (metrics server / requests mancanti / limiti) e ripristina l'autoscaling.
